source_quotes.text: The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:

Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.

For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC.

assumptions: The express effective date governs the general statement that the measures take immediate effect.
Whether an existing application remains unapproved is assessed at the effective date.
For this proposal, retention in the existing approval process excludes the pending application from the new removal of prior approval.
The stated home-supervision rationale does not add a distinct approval or supervision test to item (ii)'s express home-jurisdiction compliance condition.
The absent FAQs may qualify implementation; this is a reading of the supplied text only.
hypotheses.controlled_language: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Within scope, true means the selected material investment change qualifies for removal of SFC prior approval under item (ii), on the proposed transition reading: the assessment is on or after 28 November 2025, home requirements are met, no novel or complex product features or possible local policy implications are involved, and no pre-effective pending application retains the existing process. False means this particular removal is unavailable under this reading; it does not independently establish an approval obligation or non-compliance. Unknown inputs remain unknown. Continuing notification and post-vetting obligations are outside this predicate.
opposing_reasons: Does the transition preserve substantive approval requirements as assumed, or only administrative processing?
What further qualifications do the referenced FAQs place on the selected removal?
